subject.title: Feature: Inject post-install/update system event into active session

question: Should ClawHub introduce a consented, session-targeted post-install/update handoff for package-authored setup guidance, and what actions may that handoff request without further user approval?
rationale: The implementation crosses the boundary between a registry install operation and an agent session that may change local configuration, install plugins, or restart services; source-level work cannot safely choose that authority and failure contract alone.

options.title: Approve a consented handoff contract
options.body: Emit a structured install/update event only to an explicitly active session, with visible approval for consequential setup actions and a non-blocking failure path.

options.title: Keep setup manual
options.body: Continue treating `SKILL.md` guidance and lifecycle steps as user-initiated instructions rather than automatically delivering them into an agent session.

options.title: Limit the scope to registration diagnostics
options.body: Address missing hook or plugin registration warnings separately without creating a general agent-session execution handoff.

recommendation.title: Approve a consented handoff contract
recommendation.body: Emit a structured install/update event only to an explicitly active session, with visible approval for consequential setup actions and a non-blocking failure path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their collaborator comment is the clearest available evidence of ownership of the pending prioritization and product-boundary decision.
